rows.english: What does the body of an inbetween being look like? The being between death and rebirth has the image of the being "before," or the being which is going to come into existence. This expression, the "being before," is meant to refer to the one that consists of the five (or four) heaps that exist before the point that one has already died (up through the moment of death) but after the moment of birth (the second moment of birth and so on).

Inbetween beings for the form realm are white. No intermediate being exists for the formless realm, as there is no form there.

rows.english: Here is the first. The non-Buddhist school known as "Those who Reject the World," and other such groups as well, note the fact that there are things--like the patterns on a peacock--which don't seem as if anyone at all has made them; they say: Consider the roughness of a lotus petal, and its texture or other such qualities; think as well of the sharpness of a thorn, or the like. They just happen by their own nature; it's not as if someone made them that way. Your idea though is incorrect. This is because we can most often see--even with that direct perception which is shared throughout the world--all the causes that create the vast majority of inner and outer working things, such as crops and the like. And the great variety of results--that is, things like the colors of the stem of a lotus, or the number of petals it has--are all caused by a great variety of different causes. If you ask what it is then that causes all the different varieties of causes themselves; the answer is that they come from none other than a previous set of a great variety of causes.

rows.english: Thus should the practitioner proceed, making a thorough investigation of the essential nature of each and every object that their mind may fly forth to embrace. And in none of them will they find any essential nature at all. There will come a time then when—as they fail to find any such nature—the meditator completes their examination of all the things there are, and comes to the realization that each and every one is the same as a length of bamboo: there is no core there at all. With this, they will be able to turn their mind away from all these things.

rows.english: The House of the Jewel Trees as well speaks of a special kind of quicksilver called “the golden transformation.” A single ounce of this liquid has the power to turn a thousand ounces of iron into gold; but even this quantity of iron can not exhaust the quicksilver. This metaphor is used to explain how all the iron of our karma and negative emotions is powerless to exhaust the quicksilver core of our Wish for enlightenment.

rows.english: And so suppose that you fantasize (which is to say, believe) that we take a seed which has already grown, and plant it again, and then it grows. What reason could you ever give then for saying that—once you had planted a seed, and it had grown and then stopped, and then from that the sprout had grown (all according to you)—the seed was prevented from growing once more? There could in fact be no such reason. And as such, it would then have to be the case, in the whole world here, that we could never observe, at all, instances where sprouts & such (which is meant to include things like the trunks of trees, and the channels inside them) ever grew. Things would grow themselves forever

rows.english: It's very difficult for those who are just starting out to right away feel a deep belief for each and every teaching of the Buddha.  As such, we should follow the advice of the Levels of the Bodhisattva, where it says that "There's no problem if they don't believe it; as long as they don't discount it." This same point is made in the root tantra of Highest Bliss" Living beings possess a wide variety of propensities; And so They teach them a variety of activities. They teach a wide variety of different methods To beings, in a whole variety of ways. What They teach is a Dharma that's profound; And so even if it doesn't attract us immediately, We should never think of disparaging it-- Remind yourself how inconceivable The nature of things really is: If there's something that we can't get just yet, It's because we don't grasp reality. These great beings, the Buddhas And Their daughters and sons, Know perfectly what we need. The Jewel of Realizations and the String of Jewels also state that there is no problem if we simply leave, for the time being, a teaching which we cannot yet accept; it's a crucial point of practice for us to understand this.  The sixth of the root downfalls is to give up then any Dharma of the three different ways. *** We return to the String of Shining Jewels, for the seventh root downfall:

rows.english: For the pushpe, make your hands into diamond fists, facing up, and imagine that you are spreading flowers. rows.english: When you do this practice, you can offer your body either after it has been separated from the mind, or without being separated.  However, to offer it before the mind has left is best.  As has been explained in the classical texts on termination, you should reflect in the following way: In the past I have taken on countless bodies and each of them I have wasted with no great purpose.  But now, this time that I have been born with a body and mind of both leisure and fortune, I will quickly become a Buddha so that I may be able to free all those beings who have been my mother.  And so that I may be able to do this, I will finally do something meaningful with one of my bodies, by offering it to my Lama. When you reach the point that says, "I visualize my mind as the Angel of Diamond ..." visualize that your mind, which is the vam syllable at your heart, becomes the Angel of Diamond no larger than a thumbnail, and you travel through the central channel and emerge from the tip of your head.  Then staying in mid-air turn around and fix your stare upon your now normal body, which then falls down unconscious on its back--like a tree which has just been cut down.

rows.english: Now people have taken a lot of different positions on just what a dogupa tree is.  The Lords of Quicksilver, father and son, have though expressed the opinion that it is in actuality what the medical texts call a dowa tree.  This tree has yellow-colored flowers that looks like the pandit hats with a fold to them, and can be found scattered widely across the countryside here in Tibet.  It has a thick trunk with a hollow in the center about the width of your forefinger.  This then, they say, is the dogupa.

Some though are strung or tied into garlands, while others form a patchwork of colors, mixed in profusion.

rows.english: And the expression "thousand petals," being a poeticism for the lotus, again recalls the line in scripture which reads, "...like the sprout of a lotus flower at the edge of the sea of wishes."  That is, the collection of goodness that we have done is similar to the spreading sprouts or blooms of a lotus upon the surface of the sea. rows.english: Here is a summary of the string of metaphors here.  The offering of our personal store of virtue--the offering of a cause, really--is being compared to a sea.  Pure white deeds, whether they relate still to the cycle of suffering, or to that which is beyond this circle, are being compared to the sprouts or stems of lotuses which grow at the two shores or edges of the sea.  The good deeds of our acts, words, and thoughts are being compared to the flower blooms.  Performing these deeds with a state of mind imbued with extraordinary spiritual means is being compared to the fragrance of the flowers.   And then the three trainings, the two levels, and the five paths are being compared to the fruits that follow the flowers.
